prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Pearland, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1412; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement is about the collision you were involved in on the roadway in Pearland, Texas. Do you understand that this call is being recorded?

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Can you describe where you were driving and what the traffic was like when the collision happened?

A: I was driving southbound on the main road near the shopping center. Traffic had slowed down because of a light ahead, so I had come to a stop behind a white sedan.

Q: How long were you stopped before the impact?

A: Maybe five or six seconds. I was waiting for the cars in front to start moving again.

Q: What happened next?

A: I felt a hard jolt from behind. My head snapped back and then forward, and my seatbelt locked up across my chest. The other driver's bumper pushed my car into the sedan in front of me.

Q: Did you notice any injuries right away?

A: Not at first. I thought I was just shaken up. By that evening my neck was stiff, and by the next morning I had sharp pain in my neck and upper back that moved into my shoulders. I also had headaches.

Q: Have you seen a medical provider since the collision?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic the next day, and then I started physical therapy. The doctor said it looked like whiplash, and I've been doing exercises and taking prescribed medication.

Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?

A: Yes. Turning my head to check my blind spot is difficult, and I can't sit at my desk for long without pain.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: No, I think that covers it. I just want to get my car fixed and get back to normal.

Q: Thank you for your cooperation. This concludes the recorded statement.
